items.explanation: Playwright John Osborne (Look Back in Anger, 1956) and novelist Kingsley Amis (Lucky Jim, 1954) were the leading figures of the 1950s "Angry Young Men," whose works voiced working- and lower-middle-class disillusionment with post-war British establishment society.

items.title: Q3 · Dec 2014 (Paper II)
items.meta: Caroline & Commonwealth / Puritan Interregnum · unit-4-non-fictional-prose · John Milton
items.stem: Which of the following statement is NOT true of Areopagitica ?

structured.lead: Which of the following statement is NOT true of Areopagitica ?
structured.options_hint: It was published in 1644 It argues for t

options: It argues for the liberty of Unlicensed Printing
It pleads for British privileges regarding Free Trade
It is a speech addressed to the Parliament of England
items.explanation: John Milton's Areopagitica (1644) is a passionate prose polemic addressed to the English Parliament defending freedom of the press and opposing the Licensing Order of 1643; it has nothing to do with commercial free trade privileges.

items.title: Q4 · Dec 2014 (Paper II)
items.meta: Late Victorian, Aestheticism & Fin-de-Siecle · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story · Thomas Hardy
items.stem: Thomas Hardy's last major novel was _______

structured.lead: Thomas Hardy's last major novel was _______
structured.options_hint: Tess of the D'urbervilles Jude the Obscu

items.explanation: Published in 1895, Jude the Obscure was Thomas Hardy's last completed novel; the harsh public and critical outcry over its treatment of marriage, religion, and sexuality led Hardy to abandon novel-writing for poetry.

items.explanation: Written in 1687 by Matthew Prior and Charles Montagu, The Hind and the Panther Transvers'd to the Story of the Country Mouse and the City Mouse is a burlesque satire mocking John Dryden's Roman Catholic beast fable The Hind and the Panther (1687).

structured.lead: In King Lear who among the following speaks in the voice of Poor Tom ?
structured.options_hint: Kent Edgar Edmund Gloucester

items.explanation: In William Shakespeare's King Lear, Gloucester's legitimate son Edgar disguises himself as the naked Bedlam beggar "Poor Tom" after being framed by his bastard brother Edmund, speaking in feigned madness on the storm-swept heath.

items.title: Q8 · Dec 2014 (Paper II)
items.meta: British Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry · William Wordsworth

structured.lead: In Wordsworth's Prelude the Boy of Winander is affected by
structured.options_hint: Blindness Deafness Muteness Lameness

items.explanation: In Book V of William Wordsworth's The Prelude, the Boy of Winander mimics the hooting of owls across Windermere lake until sudden intervals of silence—and his own premature death at age twelve—leave him in the "mute" stillness of the churchyard grave.

items.title: Q9 · Dec 2014 (Paper II)

structured.options_hint: After Leaving Mr. Mackenzie Good Morning

items.explanation: The Quiet American (1955) is an anti-imperialist novel by Graham Greene set in French Indochina, whereas After Leaving Mr. Mackenzie (1931), Good Morning, Midnight (1939), and Wide Sargasso Sea (1966) were all written by Dominican-British novelist Jean Rhys.

items.title: Q11 · Dec 2014 (Paper II)

structured.lead: The first official royal Poet Laureate in English literary history was _______
structured.options_hint: Ben Jonson William Davenant John Dryden

items.explanation: John Dryden was appointed the first official Poet Laureate of England by King Charles II via royal letters patent in 1668, whereas earlier court poets like Ben Jonson and William Davenant held the role only unofficially.

Nor marrying discord in a noble wife,
Stranger to civil and religious rage,

items.stem:
"The boast of heraldry, the pomp of power,

And all that beauty, all that wealth e'er gave,

Awaits alike the inevitable hour

The paths of glory lead but to the grave."

What is the subject of awaits ?

structured.lead:
"The boast of heraldry, the pomp of power,
And all that beauty, all that wealth e'er gave,
Awaits alike the inevitable hour
The paths of glory lead but to the grave."
What is the subject of awaits ?
structured.options_hint: Hour The things mentioned in the first 2

options: The things mentioned in the first 2 lines
And all that beauty, all that wealth e'er gave
items.explanation: Through poetic inversion in Stanza 9 of Thomas Gray's "Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard" (1751), the singular noun phrase "the inevitable hour" (death) serves as the grammatical subject of the singular verb "awaits," while the worldly glories of the first two lines are its objects.

items.explanation: In these opening lines from William Drummond of Hawthornden's sonnet "To His Lute," the grammatical sense flows continuously from the first line into the second without a terminal punctuation pause, making it an example of a run-on line (enjambment).
